quotes.excerpt: we have a bad lull or a bad stretch and then now we're playing from a 10-15 point deficit
quotes.quote: We are still competing every day. We are just trying to find one. It is as simple as that. We have to search and try to find one. quotes.speaker: Zach LaVine
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach LaVine on the team's recurring third-quarter struggles
quotes.excerpt: it's been more of our MO than any other quarter. I don't know if team teams are jumping on us
quotes.quote: It's been more of our MO than any other quarter. I don't know if team teams are jumping on us, if they're being more aggressive. We have to hang our hat on something to where we come out third quarter, even throughout the whole game. Our identity offensively, defensively, what are we going for? I think I said that earlier this year, and times throughout the most of the game, it feels like we're playing randomly. That's just not going to work throughout the 48 minutes of an NBA game where teams are going at certain things and matchups.

quotes.speaker: Zach LaVine
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach LaVine on head coach's efforts to keep the team together
quotes.excerpt: he's doing his best, just like the rest of us. He hasn't changed his demeanor
quotes.quote: He is doing his best, just like the rest of us. He hasn't changed his demeanors. He is still coming in talking. I know it's as frustrating for him as it is for all of us. I don't know his struggles. I've never been a head coach before. I wouldn't want to be in that situation. I don't see myself coaching, but it's a tough job, man. I think he's doing it to the best of his abilities, just like the rest of us. I don't think anyone was trying to fail. He's holding it together.

quotes.speaker: Zach LaVine
quotes.summary_phrase: Zach LaVine on dealing with negative outside noise
quotes.excerpt: there's not a lot of positive things to say. Call a spade a spade. We're 1-13
quotes.quote: There's not a lot of positive things to say. Call a spade a spade. We're 1-13. What besides us looking at film and looking at the good things we do, the public is not going to see that. quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the team's lack of sustainable execution
quotes.excerpt: how can we put together 48 minutes of sustainable basketball that allows us to to compete
quotes.quote: I think there's a level of frustration obviously because we all want to win. I think when talking to a couple of the guys, coaches and players, part of it is the sustainability of what we do. We show it that okay, we can compete, here we are, and then all of a sudden, whether it's zero pass shots, the pace of execution, all those little tiny things, they just rear their head. And that is that you got to look in the mirror and you got to say to yourself, how can we put together 48 minutes of sustainable basketball that allows us to to compete.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the team's lack of sustainable execution: You have to look in the mirror and you have to say to yourself, how can we put together 48 minutes of sustainable basketball that allows us to compete.

structured.context: Doug Christie explains the team's difficulty in maintaining sustainable execution throughout a full 48-minute game.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the mental fortitude required to break through
quotes.excerpt: that's why you have to break through and that's what I told them the mental fortitude
quotes.quote: That's why you have to break through and that's what I told them the mental fortitude and the discipline that it takes to break through because you're right, when that happens all of a sudden you think like, oh, here we go again. You can't do that. You just you can't. That's that's going to be part of the game. That's going to happen from time to time, but you just go back and you execute because the our execution has to be at a higher level.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the mental hurdle of losing: When that happens all of a sudden you think like, oh, here we go again. You cannot do that. That is going to be part of the game, but you just go back and you execute.

structured.context: Doug Christie discusses the mental fortitude and discipline required for the team to overcome game-time adversity.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the discipline required to execute consistently
quotes.excerpt: That's the discipline. The discipline is, oh, we were spraying the basketball, oh, we were executing splits, got a back

text_blocks.speaker: Unidentified reporter
text_blocks.text: That's an easy one, but how did you get there before that?

text_blocks.speaker: Doug Christie
text_blocks.text: That's the discipline. The discipline is, oh, we were spraying the basketball, oh, we were executing splits, got a back door, we were pushing the tempo. Obviously, you got to get stops and get out and push the basketball, but how you got to that, too many times, it's so easy for us to go away from how we got there. How we got there is what's going to keep us there and ultimately go over it. And to be quite frank with you, sometimes that's boring. It's just you got to do it again, groundhog day over and over and over and over.

quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the monotony of NBA discipline: How we got there is what is going to keep us there. To be quite frank with you, sometimes that is boring. It is just you have to do it again, groundhog day over and over.

structured.context: Doug Christie emphasizes that consistent execution requires repetitive discipline, even when the process feels monotonous.

quotes.speaker: Doug Christie
quotes.summary_phrase: Doug Christie on the team's resilience and future outlook
quotes.excerpt: tough times don't last, tough people do. And this is a tough community
quotes.quote: I know that these fans love our team and our organization more than anything. Tough times don't last, tough people do. And this is a tough community and know that we are going to do everything that we can to make sure that when we work through this, because there's another side to this and when we get to the other side of this, they they will be happy. But going through it is difficult. I mean it's it's difficult for me, it's difficult for our guys, it's difficult for our coaches.
quotes.social_post: Doug Christie on the team's current struggles: Tough times do not last, tough people do. This is a tough community and know that we are going to do everything that we can to make sure that when we work through this, there is another side to this.

structured.context: Doug Christie shares a message of resilience for the fans while acknowledging the difficulty of the current losing streak.
